name: Sessions Health vs TherapyNotes
title: Sessions Health vs TherapyNotes: Mental Health EHR Comparison
description: Compare Sessions Health and TherapyNotes for mental health practices. See differences in pricing, features, support, and value for therapists.

summary.bottom_line: Sessions Health is the budget-friendly option with a free tier and therapist-designed simplicity. TherapyNotes is the established leader with 24/7 support, clinician-built templates, and more mature billing features. Choose Sessions Health for maximum affordability; choose TherapyNotes for robust support and behavioral health-specific workflows.

sections.heading: Sessions Health vs TherapyNotes: Overview
sections.content: Sessions Health and TherapyNotes are both purpose-built for mental health professionals, but represent different approaches. Sessions Health was founded in 2018 by a practicing psychotherapist with a focus on affordable, ethical pricing without hidden fees. TherapyNotes was founded in 2010 by a clinical psychologist (Dr. Debra Pliner) and tech expert (Brad Pliner) and has grown to be one of the most established behavioral health EHRs with comprehensive features and exceptional support. Both understand the therapeutic relationship, but TherapyNotes has more mature features while Sessions Health offers better value for budget-conscious practitioners.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Sessions Health is significantly more affordable with a free tier (up to 3 clients) and Professional plan at $39/month. TherapyNotes starts at $69/month for solo practitioners. Additional practitioners cost $29/month with Sessions Health vs. $50/month with TherapyNotes. However, TherapyNotes has cheaper claims ($0.14 each vs. $0.19-$0.25) and includes basic telehealth, while Sessions Health charges $10/month for telehealth. For low-volume practices, Sessions Health costs less; high-volume billers may find TherapyNotes' lower claim fees offset the higher base price.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: TherapyNotes excels in customer support (24/7 phone and email) and clinician-built note templates specifically designed for behavioral health documentation. It also has a mobile app and free data import. Sessions Health emphasizes transparent pricing and includes features others charge for (reminders, portal, storage). Both have outcome tracking and AI documentation options (TherapyFuel at $40/mo vs. Sessions Health AI). TherapyNotes has a more polished, mature platform; Sessions Health is simpler but may lack some advanced features.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your budget and support needs:

recommendations.when: You're a solo therapist prioritizing lowest cost, want a free tier to start, don't need phone support, or are comfortable with a simpler feature set
You value 24/7 support, want clinician-built templates, need a mobile app, or prefer a more established platform with free data migration
You've experienced price increases elsewhere and want stable, ethical pricing from a therapist-founded company

faqs.q: Which is cheaper: Sessions Health or TherapyNotes?
faqs.a: Sessions Health is cheaper: free for up to 3 clients, $39/month unlimited vs. TherapyNotes at $69/month. However, TherapyNotes has cheaper claims ($0.14 vs $0.25) and includes basic telehealth. For low-volume practices, Sessions Health costs less overall.

faqs.q: Does Sessions Health have 24/7 support like TherapyNotes?
faqs.a: No, Sessions Health offers email support only. TherapyNotes is known for exceptional 24/7 phone and email support on all plans. If responsive phone support is important, TherapyNotes is the better choice.

faqs.q: Which has better note templates for therapy?
faqs.a: TherapyNotes has more extensive clinician-built templates designed specifically for behavioral health by practicing clinicians. Sessions Health has customizable templates but may require more setup to match behavioral health workflows.

faqs.q: Can I switch from TherapyNotes to Sessions Health?
faqs.a: Yes, you can export data from TherapyNotes and import to Sessions Health. However, you'll lose 24/7 support and some advanced features. Consider whether the savings justify the trade-offs for your practice.
